entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I think that witness can testify on that. We can go to Paragraph 41 then.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on the same trip, apart from using First Class, we find the Governors' daughter being hired for a chopper at a cost of Kshs220,000 to go round New York City to see how beautiful the city was using public funds. She goes ahead to have an offsite party at a cost of 260 using public funds.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: That is 260 what? Tell us which currency?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is Kshs260,000. The same lady is transferred from the first ladies conference to Philadelphia at a cost of Kshs60,000. As she was in Philadelphia, she went to visit tourist sites at a cost of Kshs120,000 using Kenyan money. She was accompanied by the media. Those media people were paid Kshs120,000. While she was around that place, they were able to spend around Kshs300,000 on ground transport. However, you remember she was flown at a cost of Kshs60,000 to Philadelphia, but ground transport within Philadelphia cost Kshs300,000.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: The documents that you have referred to, do they demonstrate where these colossal amounts came from? Who paid for that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it was paid for by the County Government.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Was that payment a valid payment? Was it supposed to be paid, and was she supposed to have received such particular benefits?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, part of the money was given direct to the airline through the agent who procured the tickets. On the per diem of Kshs2.6 million, a junior officer from the county was forced to go and withdraw using her name in a company of a bodyguard of the Governor. After withdrawing the cash, the bodyguard walked away with the Kshs2.6 million.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: On this, you have indicated that there is evidence that you wanted to be played. That is in Paragraph 40 of your statement. There is a video you wanted to be played.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have clip seven.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, maybe clip seven can be played. With your comfort, it does not have any derogatory remarks.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is a party mode, I believe.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Laughter)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: I will take you to Paragraphs 41and 42. Kindly explain to the House. Kindly explain to us because it is a bit funny. Who is that? I may not know him. What was he doing?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you remember as the children of Nairobi were going home without food, others were out of school as a result of the diversion of their school fees, the Governor was in France doing party after party at the expense of service delivery in the County of Nairobi.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, thank you. Proceed to Paragraphs 41 and 42 of your statement, kindly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is about persistent harassment and intimidation of officers and the County Executive Committee (CEC) Members. This includes blackmailing his CECs and Chief Officers (Cos) with one-year contracts, whose renewal he undertakes arbitrarily, leaving the officers jittery about their employment and creating a climate of fear, uncertainty and despondence. To put this to perspective, the governor failed to renew the contract of 23 Chief Officers in May, 2019. This is a serious problem we have in the county. As MCAs, we have really tried to talk about it. You will appreciate that the Nairobi City County is where 90 per cent of officers are in acting capacity. For example, I isolated the Finance Department. You remember that since the elections, we have been in office for about 40 months. You will be shocked that during this time in the finance docket alone, we have had 10 CECs. That is within three years. We have had eight Chief Officers in the same docket. Mr. Speaker, Sir, that clearly talks about poor governance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: An Hon. Senator
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Continue. You will have your time to cross- examine

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, in regard to that, we will have one witness who will speak to that once I am done. Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your permission, we have Video No.3.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What was happening in that video clip, if it is within your knowledge?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is Ms. Janet Ouko, the then CEC for Education in the County, clearly describing the environment in which she was working.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: You will confirm that she is also a witness in this matter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, kindly let us go to Paragraph 43 of your statement. What are you telling us in short?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor has not only sexually molested female Members of the County Executive, including his CECs and Chief Officers, as shall be demonstrated later, but has extended his detestable behavior to our women, including female leaders, by publicly exposing them to ridicule, odium contempt and embarrassment. For example, in Video No.1.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your permission, Video No.1 can be played.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Kindly explain that embarrassing situation.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that was brought in order to show how H.E. the Governor treats fellow leaders, especially women.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: I will take you to Paragraph 44.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor violated Article 73 of the Constitution by failing to promote public confidence in the integrity of the Office of the Governor following his arrest and being charged for conspiracy to commit an offence of corruption to Section 47 (a) (3), as read together with Section 48 of the Anti-Corruption and Economic Crimes Act for knowingly conspiring to commit an offence of corruption, namely, embezzlement of public funds in the sum of Kshs357 million. As a consequence, the Governor has been barred from accessing his office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What do you have to demonstrate to that? Is it in your evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It is on Page 1154 and 1155.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is on the file labeled 9D. On page 1155 and 1156, kindly, explain to us quickly what you find in that particular document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Those are charge sheets as evidence of him having been charged.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Read for us the particulars of the offence in Page 1154. Who has been charged?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Kindly just read the names on Page 1154.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have Kioko Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko Mike Sonko alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko alias Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon Kioko---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: That is okay. Who are those people?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: One and the same person.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Who is that person with all those names in relation to these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: They are referring to the Gov. Sonko.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Which is the charge; Count No.1, on the same page?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Conspiracy to commit an offence of corruption.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: I will take you to the next page. That is Page 1158. On Count No. 4, what is the statement of offence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Conflict of interest contrary to Section 42 (3) as read together with Section--- Particularly, the name is Kioko Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko Mike Sonko alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko alias Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon Kioko alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko Sonko.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Okay. Count No.11, what is the statement of offence? It is on Page 1161.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Money laundering.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Again, who has been charged?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Kioko Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko Mike Sonko alias Mike Sonko Mbuvi.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: That is okay. Page 1162, Count No.13. What is the statement of offence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Acquisition of proceeds of crime contrary to Section 4 of the proceeds.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Who has been charged?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Kioko Mike Sonko Mbuvi Gideon alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko alias Mbuvi Gideon Kioko alias Mike Sonko Mbuvi.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Who is this who has been charged in relation to these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor of Nairobi County.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Go to Page 1154. Kindly, state the court case number on the top left, the third sentence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Case No.32 of 2019.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Which date?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: 9th December, 2019.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Confirm that, that is a period that the Governor was still serving as the Governor of this particular county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Go back your statement, Paragraph 45. You wanted this particular House to do what?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: He is incapable of performing his functions under Article 179 (4) of the Constitution as read together with Section 30 of the County Governments Act.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: I am referring you to Paragraph 44. There is a video clip that you intended to be played. Speak to the microphone.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Video clip No.8.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, kindly allow video clip No. 8 to be played with your permission?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Who is the flashy person in that particular video?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is the Governor of Nairobi City County.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Thank you. I will refer you to Paragraph 46. It speaks for itself.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The governor has further violated Article 73 of the Constitution and Section 8 and 11 of the Leadership and Integrity Act, 2012 on Public Trust and Professionalism, where he is on record admitting that he was intoxicated (not in the right frame of mind) when he signed the deed of transfer for the transfer of certain functions of the county to the national Government. In his own words, he did say: " Hawa watu wa State House walini-confuse na pombe . By the time I was meeting the President for that signing, I was just seeing zigzag".

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Do you have anything to demonstrate that? Do you have any video to be played on Paragraph 46?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, we have Video No. 5.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Thank you. Mr. Speaker, Sir. With your permission, kindly, allow Video No.5 to be played.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: We need volume, kindly. It is not over. It was a better quality, but that is what it is. Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu, what was that particular clip speaking to, very briefly? It was of better quality, but that is what it is. Hon. Ogada, what was that clip speaking to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, what I see is a sober person sitting comfortable and signing a document in front of you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, and His Excellency the President. I hope you will not confirm to us that he was actually drunk when you were standing behind him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: In terms of the words, I know it was not very clear. We can pack that for now. Let us go to paragraph 48.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor has always been unavailable even before he was charged in the law courts and barred from accessing the office. In the earlier days, it can be confirmed that he was conducting his activities from his home based in Machakos, which is outside the jurisdiction of the County of Nairobi. He was elected to represent the people of Nairobi, but he was conducting the affairs from Mua, which is outside the county. We refer to Video no. 4.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What is the violation in terms of gazettement? I can see you have indicated 'gazetted county boundaries.'

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It is outside the gazetted county boundaries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your permission, Video No.4, a few videos are remaining.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: That speaks to itself; it is self-evident. Let us go to Paragraph 50 of your statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Governor has on account of locations violated Article 73 and Article 75 of the Constitution and Section 8 of the Leadership and Integrity Act 2012 on public trust, where he has constantly used his position to abuse public trust in county government by persistent use of abusing, embarrassing, inappropriate and unprintable words, which undermines and greatly demeans the office.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What do you have to demonstrate that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Video 6.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Video 6, with your permission.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Kindly explain what you can hear and what you know about that video.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is basically about the language of the Governor, who should be setting a good example to the citizens of this county. In that clip, you will hear Hon. Kalembe Ndile saying, "wewe sio mwewe unapewa kuku ya bure." Hon. Kalembe Ndile was claiming that the Governor refused to pay for the food he has been consuming in the same place.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Let us go to Paragraph 54 as we wind up. What do you generally speak about that paragraph?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is in the public domain that the Hon. Governor was once convicted at the Mombasa Law Court in Criminal Case No.1675/1997, charge of failure to attend court; that was Mbuvi Gideon Kioko. Secondly, he was charged on Case No.1727/1996, charge of failure to attend court. The other one is Case No.1584/2000, charge of obtaining money by false pretense under the name Mike Norual Muoki Mboo. Case No.4, 2464/2000, charge of conspiracy to defraud in the name of Michael Muoki. The last one is Case No.630/98 sentenced and committed to imprisonment in Shimo la Tewa under the prison number in Mombasa. It is also on record that the Governor admitted that he escaped from lawful custody following his admission at the Coast General Hospital. That escape could only be unlawful.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What do you have to demonstrate on that particular issue?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Video No.10.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is the last video.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: What do you have to say about that bragging post by the Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, based on the evidence that we can see, we can clearly see that the Governor is used to being in custody. Basically, it is nothing strange to him. I hope that is not the best of examples that we need to set for our children. The only thing that we request this honourable House is to help and save Nairobians to have focused leadership.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: I will refer you to the documents on the affidavit. You can look at it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Kindly, speak to that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: These are documents dated 1st October 2010 from the Office of Vice-President and Minister of Home Affairs.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: On which date?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada
entries.text: 1st October, 2010.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Duncan Okatch)
entries.text: Read it for us.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Confidential report on Ex-Kamiti Prisoner, Mbuvi Gideon Kioko. The above referred person was a prisoner at this institution, during the period between 2000 and 2001, specifically as a convicted prisoner and a remand prisoner. From our archives, we have been able to compile the person's records at this institution as given below. True certified copies of the record are enclosed herein as well. Mr. Speaker, Sir, from the documents before us, I can see that the date of escape from the Shimo la Tewa Prison is 16th April, 1998.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is the date of escape of who and from where.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That date indicated, 16th April, 1998, is the date of escape from Mike Mbuvi Gideon Kioko from Shimo la Tewa Prison. There is also a date of recapture indicated as 17th November, 2000.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, Mr. Ogada has elucidated a lot about the grounds of your accusation. To that extent, I would like to ask you in passing about the diversion of funds meant for bursaries. Why do you blame the Governor for that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Governor is basically the CEO of the county and oversees everything that takes place within the county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, how do you connect the Governor to the issue of Dandora Stadium and the indictment by the PPRA? How do you connect the Governor to that particular indictment?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Governor is the CEO and has several advisors, both from the technical team and the PPRA. The only thing that he could do to save Nairobians is to make sure that the stadium was done according to specifications without giving in to the so called cartels, by allowing them to change and vary documents at will. Verification was done when the stadium was downgraded from the concrete terraces, while the cost of the tender remained the same. The Nairobi City County Government in the end lost colossal amounts of monies.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, in short, what would be your closing remarks based on the evidence that you have adduced?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, mine is to request this honorable House as the defenders and the protectors of devolution to rise to the occasion and ensure that devolution is defended and protected. The only thing that this House can do to assist the residents of Nairobi County who have been groaning is by ensuring that the monies being transferred for devolved functions are being used for the same functions that they have been made for. The one thing that I would like to put across is that we have put our case with very good pieces of evidence. The only thing we request of this honorable House is to rise to the occasion because devolution is the business of this House. The Nairobi City County Assembly has done its part. We have ensured that the Governor is held accountable.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, what can you say about documentary evidence that you have referred to? Would you want those to be adduced as evidence in this particular Motion as your personal evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would want all the evidence we brought yesterday to be admitted as evidences, including the documentary evidences.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that will be end of examination-in-chief.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, before the closure of the examination-in-chief, I would like to go on record that we have objected to the production of those documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Proceed to cross-examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, did Mr. Ogada swear an affidavit before this Senate to affirm that what he is telling this honourable Senate is the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, yes, I swore an oath.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Where is your oath, Mr. Ogada? The longer we take on this issue the more time we waste. Do you have an oath that you can pinpoint that you took?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have my witness statement clearly indicated and filed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the fact is that Mr. Ogada has not sworn an affidavit. Mr. Ogada clearly stated in his evidence-in-chief that he made the statement on 3rd November, 2020. Is that right? In his introductory remarks, Mr. Ogada said that he made his witness statement on a certain date. Is that right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I stated that we prosecuted the impeachment Motion on 3rd December, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that means that the statement that Mr. Ogada is relying upon is not dated. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I think that once a personal statement is signed, that is good enough.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The statement is not dated.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the statement is signed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Answer my question.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the statement is signed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have an equivalent statement, an affidavit or witness statement that you made before the Nairobi City County Assembly before, on or subsequent to 3rd December, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, what I had in the Nairobi City County Assembly was a Motion that---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, show some respect to this honourable House and the Nairobi City County Assembly. Did you or did you not have a similar witness statement before the county assembly on, before or immediately subsequent to 3rd December, 2020?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I had a Motion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this witness is being dodgy and the longer we take with these sort of responses, the more difficult it is for us to make useful time of what it actually---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it would be important for the witness to be protected from harassment. He has answered that question several times.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: May I ask you, Mr. Ogada. Did you or did you not have a witness statement before the Nairobi City County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have said that I did a Motion and that is the procedure. We do not do statements in the Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, I will come to the Motion. Do you or do you not have a statement?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is not the procedure of the county assembly to have statements. We do Motions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, which Standing Order are you relying on? Please, do not waste time. I am asking you because you are a witness and your advocates are assisting you. You want the Governor to lose his seat on account of your evidence. Please, listen to my question. I would like to demonstrate utmost respect to your seat and honourable Members. If he does not answer the question, the longer it takes for us to move forward because it is relevant to the Governor because he lamented that he has never been served with any statement of a similar nature. I will take it that the witness has declined to answer the question, which bears relevance. Mr. Ogada, if you look at your Statement, it is addressed to the Senate and the hon. Speaker.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Rose Nyamunga Ogendo
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Nyamunga.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Rose Nyamunga Ogendo
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. As we continue with the proceedings, the lawyer for the Governor should be addressing you and not the witness because that is a bit of intimidation. The procedure of the House is addressing the Chair is to address the Chair.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay. Proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, hon. Member, I did not mean to intimidate you because counsel was looking and addressing the witness of Nairobi City County Assembly. Are you familiar with Standing Order No.67 of the County Assembly Standing Orders?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, that is the procedure for removal of Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor (Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui)
entries.text: I am asking whether you are aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I am.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: It is required that the Notice of Motion shall be signed by the Member who affirms that the particulars of allegations contained in the Motion are true to his knowledge, and the same verified by each of the Members consisting at least a third of all the Members of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, Sure.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You look at the Motion dated 25th November, 2020. Did you sign it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, sure.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor (Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui)
entries.text: Did you sign it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Notice of Motion to the Speaker was signed by me.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Does it contain an affirmation that the particulars of allegations contained in the Motion are true to your knowledge. Does it contain that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, it has.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor (Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui)
entries.text: Show us where it contains that. There is nowhere in your Notice of Motion containing that affirmation. Mr. Okumu, you have not answered my question. You are being dodgy. Is it not true that His Excellency the Governor on 23rd November complained about you embezzling Nairobi City County Funds on account of a trip that you were to make to Dubai, but you did not travel.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is an irrelevant question.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Answer the question; Yes or No?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Listen to me when I am talking. Those are irrelevant things, they are sideshows. I said he was paid Kshs300 million in the county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order! If you speak at the same time, I will not follow what you are saying. Be systematic.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I beg that this witness is asked all manner of questions. The only interruptions were implicating, before you no more than four interruptions. Instead of the witness answering, he is saying we are being dodgy. Is he in a particular way aware that this was lodged against him? If he can answer, we will be brief. Let me repeat my question so that we can save time. It is true that there was in fact a complaint made against you by His Excellency the Governor on 23rd November, 2020 with the Directorate of Criminal Investigation (DCI) that you had received money in purported travel to Dubai, but you never travelled.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that is a sideshow and an irrelevant issue to this House. Number one, he understands the issue of imprests. It is totally outside what we are doing here. It is irrelevant.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is a relevant question which goes to motive and character. Sorry---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Linturi?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Franklin Mithika Linturi
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am kindly asking you to protect the lawyer of the Governor when he is asking questions to make sure they answered. The questions being raised have a serious dimension on his character and integrity. If he can do that, how is the Senate required to trust and believe what he is saying? It is important for him to answer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay. Witness, try to answer what you are asked as precisely as possible.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on the issue he is raising of a trip to Dubai, I have been an MCA for donkey years, starting from being a councillor and nothing has been raised against me. I have never been involved in any criminal activities, neither have I been arrested. In any case, an imprest of a safari in the month of December, I was prosecuting this case so that I can travel. However, they are trying to make it look like I did not travel, which is not the case. We understand the issue of imprest. According to the policy, you have to surrender it within 12 months. Within a week---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Sen . Olekina
entries.text: On a point order, Mr. Speaker, Sir

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Olekina?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is the Senate of the Republic of Kenya and we are performing an important function. We are here to defend the interest of counties and their governments. It would be proper that when the witness is responding to questions to substantiate. I have heard the witness say that he is supposed to surrender imprest within 12 months. However, the PFM Act is clear. You surrender imprest within seven days on return from a trip. If the witness can respond to the question asked by the lawyer, it will help us. We are listening and would like to follow. First, I want to know whether the statement was signed. I am still lost. It would be proper for us to know the character of the witness to determine whether this is true. We can be fabricating things here or be confused in following the procedures. I would like to request that you direct the witness to respond to questions as asked, so that we can follow. We are not able to make notes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is what I have directed. In any case, whatever answer he gives, it will assist you to make an opinion on how the witness is. If he is not responding to what has been asked, take note and you will raise it when the time comes and we are making the judgement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, on behalf of the County Assembly, we will seek your indulgence and guidance as to when the character evidence is called into question. The rules of evidence are clear. The Evidence Act bears us witness. For the moment, you open up to the character of a witness it also invites your character to be put into question. We were told and you gave a ruling that we shall not have an opportunity of cross-examining the Governor. Where shall we rebut the character evidence of our witness if we shall not have the Governor on the stand? There must be equality of arms if character evidence is called into question, we must be given an opportunity to rebut it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon Members, this hon. House was treated to an array of clips and audio tapes. This witness said that we look at the character of the Governor and assault him on that score, but he is not prepared to answer the issue about his own conduct at the county assembly being referred to by the Director of Criminal Investigations (DCI) on account of his embezzlement of money. He says that this is a side show. That is his response. Like they say, we must have equality of arms. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Wetangula?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: My learned friend, Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui, is a very experienced lawyer. I would want to encourage him to cross examine the witness; do not engage in arguments with him. He should ask him questions, wait for an answer, and move on. When you engage in an altercation with a witness, both of you look like you are not in a court of law. So just ask him questions and do not bother drawing conclusions for us; we shall draw them. You are here to ask questions to the witness and find out what you want to find out, to help the House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Let me proceed. Hon. Ogada, is it true that you received Kshs823, 324 to travel to Dubai on a trip on 23rd October, 2020? Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is very correct.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, did you receive from Nairobi City County Assembly Kshs823, 324 shillings to travel to Dubai?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Just answer. Just answer, is it yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, did you travel to Dubai? Mr. Ogada, did you travel to Dubai?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Your microphone has a problem, because we cannot---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, what I am saying is that we are engaging in a side show. That is a side show.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Just answer the question so that we are able to make progress.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as the Vice Chairperson of the Budget Committee, the members of the Budget Committee and I was given trip to travel for study to Dubai. Due to the engagement, I did a letter to the Chief Officer Finance telling him that I will attend the next meeting because I was totally engaged in the case in front of us. So I did not manage to travel, but we agreed that I would travel for the next training.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, those are public funds that you received for a specific trip. While standing there, you have accused the Governor of misusing public funds. He allegedly pocketed public funds. He is allegedly facing criminal offences with regard to public funds. You, yourself, have you returned a penny of that money for not travelling?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru consulted loudly)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have all these whispers going on there with Mr. Njiiru. I beg your indulgence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I want to repeat this. This is a very important process in the Senate of the Republic of Kenya. The question is, should a witness be assisted by the attorney? In every question, the witness is seeking clarification from the lawyer on how to answer the question. Should we proceed like that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The attorney is there to assist the witness---

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Christopher Andrew Langat
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes, Sen. (Dr.) Langat.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Christopher Andrew Langat
entries.text: In order for us to move on, I tend to think that some questions require only a "yes" or a "no" answer. It is so simple. That does not require any consultation from somebody. These are the kinds of question where a "yes" or a "no" answer will do. It is so simple.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Witness, I have directed that you answer the questions that you are asked. Give any answer and leave the conclusions to the court. This is being recorded on the Hansard. We will look at your responses and that will assist us in arriving at a conclusion. So, just answer what you can answer. What you cannot answer, say that you are not able to answer, so that it is also on record.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I am much obliged.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I beg that during cross examination, my learned friend, Mr. Njiiru, should stay put. He will assist his witness in re-examination, if any. I have only asked four questions in a space of 22 minutes. Hon. Ogada, have you returned a penny of that money?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Erick Okong'o Mogeni
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Omogeni, what is your point of order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Erick Okong'o Mogeni
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you know we are doing ---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Your microphone is off.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Erick Okong'o Mogeni
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as Sen. Orengo rightly put it when we began these proceedings, these are time-bound proceedings. Looking at the demeanor of the witness, if it takes five minutes to answer one question which requires a "yes" or "no" answer, these proceedings may never come to an end. I urge you to remind the witness that we do not have the luxury of time. If you ask me whether I have refunded money, I will either tell you yes or no, then the Senate will draw conclusions. He should not take five minutes to answer a very simple question. It is not fair.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Let us proceed. Let us minimize the interventions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Only one guidance, Mr. Speaker, Sir, that Mr. Kinyanjui should not appear to approbate the witness so that the witness can stick to the relevancy of the question before the assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the relevancy will come in submissions. I think Mr. Njiiru is interrupting me endlessly and I stand guided. Have you returned a penny of the money that you took from the county assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, you have therefore unlawfully appropriated Kshs823, 000 from the city county assembly. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, is it true that you have been summoned by the DCI to answer on these issues?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, are you aware that the alleged Motion which you based your impeachment proceedings upon was not a live Motion because there was an earlier Motion by Hon. Peter Imwatok dated 20th February, 2020, to impeach the Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: This is a totally different Motion. It is not the same one.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Look at the date of your Motion. What is it dated?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Motion was on 3rd December.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The Motion is dated 25th November, 2020. Is that correct? Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is the Notice of Motion. The Motion was done on 3rd December.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Did that Notice of Motion have any other document accompanying it when you lodged it?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, we had the signatures of the members.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The signatures of the members?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have a copy of that before this hon. Senate?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon Michael Ogada
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes, Sen. Omogeni.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Erick Okong'o Mogeni
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, maybe I should assist counsel for the governor so that we do not waste a lot of time. All those documents are in this file including the signatures and the dates.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I wanted the witness to affirm that because that came from the Speaker of the Nairobi City County Assembly. I wanted him to pinpoint to us his own document. Mr. Speaker, Sir, there are two sets of signatures required in an Impeachment Motion, which is why I am asking. The first set is for the one third and the second set for the two thirds majority. Hon. Ogada, do you have your Impeachment Motion accompanied by any other document other than itself?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the procedure for a Notice of Motion is a thrid of the Members, which we duly did and forwarded to the Speaker. We met the threshold. The rest is for the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr.Harrision Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, are you familiar with Standing Order No. 67(5) of the Nairobi City County Assembly Standing Orders, which requires signatures in support of a Motion for removal of a governor by impeachment to be provided?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I am aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have an open space against each name for the purpose of appending signatures?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, mine was to forward a Notice of Motion. The rest is basically the work of the Speaker of the County Assembly. He looked at it and we met the threshold. The requirements as per the Stoning Orders were met. That is why we prosecuted our Motion in the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Did you furnish The governor with you evidence?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, to the best of my knowledge, the governor was furnished with all the necessary documents he required at that time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrision Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are you familiar with standing Order No. 72(2) of the County Assembly Standing Orders? Read it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It says- "The person being removed from office shall be availed with the report of the Select Committee together with any other evidence adduced and such note or papers presented to the Committee, at least three days before the debate on the Motion."

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrisson Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Did you have a select Committee on your Motion dated 25th November 2020?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have just answered and said that I met the requirements. All the other procedural issues were done.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have a special Committee report?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, all the documents from the County Assembly were forwarded to them and others were forwarded to the Senate.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is it your supposition that what Mr. Speaker has is a sum of the documents in totality for the Impeachment Motion from the Nairobi City County Assembly? Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Having met the requirements and procedures---.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Please answer 'yes' or 'no'. The totality of the documents which were submitted by the Speaker of the Nairobi City County Assembly are all that there is concerning your Motion?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Because that---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrision Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No, no, no. Please. Sen. Omogeni has said---.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order. Let us not talk at the same time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it is good if he allows me to answer. Once a Motion mover has met the requirements and the threshold and has done it in the County Assembly, the issues of communicating with the Senate is basically the work of the County Assembly Speaker. Whichever documents he forwarded are the correct ones.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, so you have no proof that the documents you allege were served on the Speaker in compliance with Standing Oder No. 72(2) of the Nairobi City County Assembly Standing Orders were served?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I do not need to have proof.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Listen and say 'yes' or 'no' kindly. Do you have any proof?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The Senate and the County Assembly know the requirements.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, do you have proof?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Ogada
entries.speaker_title: (Witness for the County Assembly)
entries.text: That is the work of the Speaker.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, allow him to respond.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is basically the work of the Clerk of the County Assembly, the Speaker of the County Assembly, the Clerk of the Senate and the Speaker of the Senate. It is not my work.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Hon. Ogada, you have referenced all these documents. For example, look at your ground one, Vol. 1, bundle 5; the thick blue file. Did you furnish the governor this bundle?

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Ndegwa Njiru) rose in his place)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi Cityt County Assembly)
entries.text: Which page are you referring to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrisson Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No, no, no. Give him and sit down. Did you furnish the governor with your Vol.1, bundle 5?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, we did and that is why---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No, no, no. Not for these proceedings. We are still at the County Assembly proceedings.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Listen to my question so that we save time. Did you furnish the governor with this bundle?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We gave the governor all the necessary documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you recall when you gave him?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is in the records of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, you have no proof that you gave him? As at the time you were making your Impeachment Motion, these were supposed to have been accompanying your own file. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is why I talked about them because they were there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You recall that your Motion is dated the 25thof November, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Look at page 404, Volume I and 405. It is perjury, wrong and against God's will and dictates and commands to lie. Therein is a copy of Court Order in Petition E/371 of 2020. Would you confirm that it is dated the 30th of November, 2020? I am sorry it is page 404 and 405.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that is an order issued by the High Court in Petition E /371 of 2020?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I can see.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: It is a lie when you allege that on the 25th of November 2020, you lodged these documents and furnished the governor with them. Please answer the question as per the Speaker's direction so that we move forward

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I can confirm that we gave the governor all the documents he required.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I am referring to page 404.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order. What is your intervention, Sen. Wako?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Amos Wako
entries.text: Thank you, very much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I think we should all remember that this is not a court of law although it is a quasi-judicial proceeding. Therefore, we should confine ourselves to the issues at hand. The line of questioning, I am now hearing that you should first of all establish whether this witness, under Standing Orders of the County Assembly--- Is what he is asking a responsibility of this witness, the Clerk or the Speaker of the County Assembly? It ought to be questioned whether that document is there or not, and so on. Mr. Speaker, Sir, to my understanding, the Leader of Minority, you normally leave it to the Speaker and Clerk to forward the documents up here. When they come here, you can again bring them on that rule. The fourth one, in order to save time, is that on some of the issues whether a document is there or not, the documents speak for themselves. It is something that can be mentioned in submissions. I am just saying this because of the time factor. I know that my learned friend can question you for two or three days. Mr. Speaker, Sir, if you can just limit to the issues at hand and realize that these are quasi-judicial proceedings and not the proceedings in a court of law. These are not criminal proceedings, if I may say so or civil proceedings. It is quasi-judicial, which more or less says that without undue regard to technicalities, focus on the issues at hand.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes, that is true. Sen. Cherargei, what is your point of intervention? A brief one because we have less than one hour.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Cherarkey K Samson
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, just a brief one. I think my learned senior, the Attorney General emeritus should have followed the thought of questioning. If I heard correctly, the counsel for the Governor was questioning just before at the level of the County Assembly. He was not questioning at the tail-end why it is here. It is important that we also follow, so that we do not get misled. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Halake, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Abshiro Soka Halake
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we need your guidance. This being a quasi- judicial process, perhaps, there is what you need to remind ourselves, as Senators and from your Chair. The kind of interruption and vested interests would have disqualified us to be even near as jury. Since we are being watched, it is for us to show impartiality as we listen, so that our vested interest do not seem to come to the fore as it is doing now. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order! We need to---

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Cherargei spoke off record)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You are off record. You do not have the microphone. Order! Take your seat. Hon. Senators, I did mention---

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Sen. Cherargei spoke off record)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I have not even said anything. I want to say something and you are saying "I cannot allow." How do you know what I am going to say? As I did indicate in the morning, we are a jury and must try as much as possible to do a lot of listening then, we will have our opinion when we meet. We will look at the evidence that we would have gotten from the listening. Let us try to minimize the interjections. As I said, we are time-bound. Proceed, Counsel.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Why do we not allow the Counsel? What is your point of order?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: John Kinyua Nderitu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are here to listen. That is why we want the questions to be asked, so that we can follow. Somebody should not assume any role. We are here to listen. You learn a lot by listening. That is why I am here keenly listening. Any question that they can ask, we are here to listen and that is why we set this day to listen, so that we can be clear in what is being discussed. We will make a decision after listening. However, nobody should insinuate sinister motive about anything that somebody asks. We are here to listen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Let us listen.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: John Kinyua Nderitu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, even watching videos, we can still watch videos.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay. Let us listen. Counsel, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, thank you very much. Just in a second, with tremendous respect to my very able legal senior, Sen. Wako. The basis and the contextual order in which I was asking that question is because the Speaker made a ruling pursuant to your Rule No.29. I had made a request for invocation of Rule No.19 for rejection of these documents. The thrust, therefore, of my cross-examination is to demonstrate using their own evidence by the County Assembly. It was not feasible to have a document dated 30th November on the 25th November to proceed with the impeachment. Mr. Speaker, Sir, therefore, I have supported that and that was the basis and the context. In other words, the subsuming of my preliminary objection into the main hearing is indifference to your ruling. I do not wish to vex you; I beg your patience.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, only one thing. The evidence that Mr. Kinyanjui is seeking to lead the witness to is actually placed contextually in a preliminary objection. You did give your direction in the morning that these matters shall be argued concurrently. When Mr. Kinyanjui coerces a witness in that manner---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am not coercing. Allow me to proceed, with respect.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: I am on my feet, Mr. Kinyanjui, if you may. The whole aspect is the question and context of the matter before us. That is what the witness is addressing. Mr. Kinyanjui is not even giving time to the witness to answer, even when the witness is candidly answering the question. He is just coercing him. We seek for the protection of our witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay. Proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have been very patient with this witness. As a record, the honourable Members will bear me out. Let me proceed. You do confirm that you also have other documents that are subsequent to in their dating the 25th November, 2020 in your bundles.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as I had said, filing documents with the Senate is basically the work of the Clerk of the County Assembly, and they did file the documents which were necessary.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are aware that you have orders that were actually in consequence of the proceedings in the High Court touching and implicating the Nairobi Metropolitan Services (NMS). Is that right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Those orders were issued subsequent to your Motion of Impeachment. Is that correct?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, since I am not the legal officer in the County Assembly, I might not know the cases which are in court. I was basically prosecuting---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: There is an intervention from the Senate Minority Leader.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am standing up because of what I had raised earlier. For the case of the County Assembly, they have hardly one hour and they have got two witnesses. Mr. Kinyanjui, the way I look at the evidence which is on record, probably he needs another two hours to cross-examine. The problem is that we did not have a pretrial process, so that there are agreed documents. For Mr. Kinyanjui, may I suggest that if you find at the tail-end he has not dealt with the substantial issues and take all his time on procedural issues. Mr. Speaker, Sir, in a trial of this nature, I wanted to propose to you that even the Evidence Act does not apply. The Evidence Act clearly states where that statute applies. Even in quasi-judicial proceedings, like the commissions of inquiry, you will find most of the time, they state clearly that the Evidence Act will not apply. In the Senate, the most important rule is the Rule of Relevance. That is a substantial rule. So long as you are relevant, even you, Mr. Speaker, Sir, cannot stop me. However, because we are time-bound--- I pity both sides because the case before us is neither being made out nor being rebutted. We are just dealing with issues that have got no substance. Article 159 of the Constitution talks about substantial justice as opposed to technicalities. As the Attorney-General emeritus has said, these are not judicial proceedings. In fact, I may say, what we are addressing here is basically a political question. Like they say in the United States of America (USA), impeachments address pollical questions. That was said even in the Gov. Wambora case. So, I would urge that we use the time usefully so that there is quality of arms. I know that we have only two hours. I guess if Mr. Ndegwa also takes the same time cross- examining the other side, by 6.30 p.m., we will be complaining that let have another day or two more hours. However, we are time bound and you cannot do it. You must report the outcome of these proceedings by Friday.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay. Sen. Wetangula, take two minutes so that we proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Masika Wetangula
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is a book called The Imaginary Invalid by Moliere, where he says in many situations, patients die out of complications arising out of the treatment they get other than the ailments they have. I want to encourage my distinguished learned juniors at the Bar, that you have issues placed before this House. Attack those issues, discount them if you can. Mr. Kinyanjui, your preliminary objection was a matter for submission and not for evidence. The witness has given evidence. Attack the evidence. You know the allegations that have been brought here. You will end up exhausting your time like Sen. Orengo said, and you have not discounted a single allegation against your client.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Ochillo-Ayacko, one minute.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Sen. (Dr). Ochillo-Ayacko
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I must declare my interest. Counsel Kinyanjui and I were in the same university at the same time and in the same class. I suggest and propose to him that you do not have to insist on yes or no. Just note that there was no answer for it. It will enable us progress so that if the witness is slow, it could be to the disadvantage of the people presenting through that witness. That way, we will be able to utilize this time effectively and efficiently.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. M. Kajwang, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Moses Otieno Kajwang'
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, when we are considering impeachment by way of a Committee, it has been established that the presentation of evidence in the four hours available, we have traditionally given three hours for the evidence in chief, 30 minutes for cross-examination and 30 minutes for the re-examination. I think that is the point that Sen. Orengo has been attempting to canvas since morning.
