Since we did not have that clarity, we must find a way of making a judicious decision that will guide us tomorrow. This is because tomorrow the Executive is supposed to present its evidence. To avoid this kind of situation, you may want to consider how to deal with today but give guidelines for tomorrow in line with the tradition that has been there in Committees.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Wamatangi, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Paul Kimani Wamatangi
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this is an issue that I have raised every time this House has had to consider impeachment of any governor. I have raised it consistently. Even the last time, I insisted that this House must address itself to Standing Order No.75(2). In addressing itself to that Standing Order, then we shall find the answer to what Sen. Orengo has raised all the time. Standing Order No.75(2) provides that "The Senate sitting in Plenary or Special Committee appointed under (1), shall within 10 days, (a) Investigate the matter (b) In the case of a special Committee or even plenary, report to the Senate on whether it finds the particulars of the allegations against the governor to have been substantiated." Mr. Speaker, Sir, I raise this matter because consistently, we have put ourselves in a straight jacket that we limit ourselves all the time. We always limit ourselves to gazetting two days. The Standing Orders are very clear that after viewing such bundles of documents and listening to the evidence, we are supposed to investigate the matter and then report even when we are sitting as a Committee of the whole House. As the matter is raised by Sen. Orengo, if we do not address ourselves subsequently to this issue, in my view, we shall never be able stand up and say that we have the matter the adequacy of time and address that it requires. We need to address that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Kipchumba Murkomen
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, before I raise the issue I want to raise, I suspect Sen. Wamatangi has misapplied himself on the provision of Standing Order No.75 because the 10 days are cumulative. That includes exchange of documents, preparation of votes and so on. Therefore, 10 days are not for the hearing. We are time bound like Sen. Orengo has ably canvassed here for the better part of these proceedings from morning. I want to suggest a practically solution to the counsel. We have only one hour and eight minutes to complete the four hours. To the counsel for the county Government, if it is okay with you to give, I will give him a suggestion on how he will share the remaining one hour and eight minutes between his two witnesses then he can allocate for cross- examination certain number of minutes to the counsel for the Governor. For the comfort of the counsel of the Governor, he needs to know that we are not in a fully court process. All the information need not to come through cross-examination. It can even come from a way of closing submissions. For as long as the information gets to these Senators, nobody is so stricto sensu following the issue of procedure, so that we save time. We are not a court of law where you follow whether the witness statement was verified or not. For as long as the information is submitted on both sides, it will be achieved. Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have only one hour and seven minutes because I have already taken one minute. How can they divide that time among themselves so that we are sure that by 7.20 p.m., when the four hours are over, they will have finished?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Lastly, let us hear the Senator Majority Leader. We are going to what we said that we shall end up talking.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Samuel Poghisio
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Majority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, just practical things. I have seen that there is a string of Senators who want clarification of questions. There is a time allotted at the end of 30 minutes or so, assume that that has been subsumed also because we are free to interrupt any time. We can run that programme concurrently, so that we do not have to wait at the end.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes, Sen. Wamatangi. Please, we must proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Paul Kimani Wamatangi
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will be very brief. I do not understand when Sen. Murkomen says that I have misapplied myself to that Standing Order. That is something very simple. I have been a Member of two Committees that have participated in the impeachment of a governor. If we gave this process to a Committee, it would have had 10 days.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I think you are not getting it right. That is not the position. Sen. Olekina, kindly, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I do not wish to differ with the Senator Majority Leader, but I want this corrected. Although this is a political process, Article 96 mandates us to protect the interest of counties and their governments. The line of questioning should be relevant on procedures. If there are things that are clearly being flouted, we need to note them. So that when we sit down, we can do our job properly by taking all matters into consideration. Mr. Speaker, Sir, so the line of questioning should be relevant on procedures so that we can do our job properly by taking all matters into consideration. On the second issue, the point of order raised by Sen. Wamatangi is quite clear. It says investigate. What time do we have to investigate? This information has to be substantiated so that when we are making a decision, it helps us. Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is no point of sitting here and rushing everything---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: (Hon. Lusaka)
entries.speaker_title: The Speaker
entries.text: You know---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Allow me to finalize. There is no point of us rushing everything as if our minds have already been determined. It is proper for us to be able to do our job as we have been sent here by people who elected us.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order Sen. Olekina. You are talking and annoying yourself for nothing.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Laughter)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You are annoying yourself for nothing. The Standing Orders are very clear. We may appreciate that the time given to handle this kind of matter is not enough. To address that, you must then look at the Standing Orders and maybe change the timings. However, for now we are time-bound.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Erick Okong'o Mogeni
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I want to make reference to the Fifth Schedule. Under Rule 22, time for Senators to ask questions is limited to two minutes. However, if you go to Rule 21, there is no capping of time for cross-examination. Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is a lacuna there and we need your intervention. Mr. Speaker, Sir, my proposal is that you invoke Rule 29 and limit time for cross- examination. Rule 29 says:- "Where no provision has been made in the Standing Orders or in these rules, the Speaker of the Senate shall rule on the question or the matter and the ruling of the Speaker shall be final." Mr. Speaker, Sir, unless you manage these proceedings, we will not be able to do it within the time permitted by the Constitution. I urge the Speaker that the way we are managing time for presentation of evidence, you also cap time for cross-examination so that we are able to do this proceedings within the constitutionally permitted time. Thank you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, you have to wind up in the next 10 minutes so that we get the other witnesses.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with all tremendous respect, this witness took so much time and yet he covered grounds that I have not had to cover on account of his intransigence, failure to answer, diversion, intervention of his counsel. It will be, with tremendous respect, unfair to the Governor. He needs to demonstrate that this process is driven by something other than the truth. I beg you to allow me, 10 minutes will truncate in unfairness. I beg because I am not the author of that eventuality, it is the witness. The documents contained herein rebut his own case and I was pointing those documents when he does not want to refer to them. Mr. Speaker, Sir, if I may with your kind permission have an enlargement of that time. Otherwise, it will be unfair because my learned friends had issues to cover. If you note, this witness was taken paragraph by paragraph almost reading his own statement.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Okay proceed. I will give you---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I think our law and the Constitution has been built out on experience. In the United Kingdom, impeachment became very unpopular. There was a governor of Bengal in India who was impeached in parliament for seven years. The two parliaments had to sit through an impeachment process for seven years. Mr. Speaker, Sir, in the United States of America, impeachment took a similar direction because they preferred the Plenary as we have now. However, out of practice, they have recognized that in order to do justice they do it through committees because Counsel would want to ask a lot of questions and then report to the House although the rules demand that they do it through Plenary. When we sit as a House, everybody is agitated and each one of us wants to undertake an intervention. If every lawyer has to take the time that he or she wants to make, then it will make a mockery of the rules and the County Governments Act. We are time bound. It reminds me of the petition of hon. Martha Karua which was delayed in the High Court and the Court of Appeal and by the time he was appealing to a superior court, they said that he took too long and that he was too late. I beg that we do justice to both parties. What we are doing right now is just rumbling and the Nairobi City County Assembly will say that they still have three more witnesses. What is the Nairobi City County Governor also take the same kind of time, then this proceeding will go beyond Friday? I insist that the Speaker should give timelines but it is unfortunately too late for that now. The Counsel of the Governor should be given more time considering the fact that the counsels for the Nairobi City County Assembly took a lot of time which they will pay for because the other witness will not have any time. The Nairobi City County Assembly have consumed fall their time on one witness. This is a question of case management. These are very senior lawyers who now have a case before the Court of Appeal. They have given us direction that we are not going to hear you. They are given a written submission of 15 pages and we are not being allowed to address the court because of case management. We cannot be rumbling and saying that we are a court. I do not think we look like a court anymore because of the interventions we are making. It is very difficult to refrain from showing where your interests lie that is why I encourage the Members of the Senate to refrain from asking questions because their interests are coming out and they are going to be the judges at the end. You cannot be a judge, a prosecutor and the executioner. It does not work that way. Let the Counsel bring their question then the witnesses give their evidence because we have the last work not even the Speaker. It is us, Senators, with the last word. I ask that we proceed in a more orderly fashion.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, I give you 20 minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, as you allocate Mr. Kinyanjui time, kindly consider giving us time for re- examination.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, you took a lot of time with your witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, allow me to congratulate the hon. Members of this House. Allow me 30 seconds to make a very weighty comment to what Sen. Orengo, who is my very senior colleague, has said. I had made reference alluding to the Impeachment Bill of 2018 and took time to look at the HANSARD where Sen. Mutula Kilonzo Jnr, made a commentary about that. I noted that had the Impeachment Bill of 2018 pursuant to Article 181(2) being legislated, hon. Members, all these would be completely gone because I would have invoked Section 16 as read with Section 14 of that Bill. But alas, the governor has been deprived that instrumentality of the law yet Schedule 5 gives 18 months from 2010 to pass that law. Having said that, I continue so that I can conclude my cross examination. Mr. Ogada do you acknowledge that you have documents dated beyond the 25th of November, 2020 that could not have been tabled before the Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, what I said is, once we gave Notice of Motion, the other documents are tabled in the Assembly during the Motion, which was on 3rd December, 2020. The documents he has been showing me were documents of November 2020. We had the documents when I was prosecuting the issue.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada are you aware that the governor is entitled to a hearing before the Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I do.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are you aware that having not been accorded a hearing it is unfair to him?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I can confirm that he was accorded a hearing and a link was sent to him which he opted not to attend.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have a video attached to the affidavit of the governor marked 'd' indicating that we had the governor's lawyer go to---If I could ask the Information Communication and Technology (ICT) technicians to play that video while I ask the next question. As we wait for the video clip to be played, are you aware that the accusations you have levelled against the governor concerning the NMS are subject of a constitutional petition? Please answer 'yes' or 'no', you heard the Hon. Members.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am not aware about the constitutional interpretation needed by the governor from the court.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are not aware? Have you not annexed a single order in your documents; the ones you are referring to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, he asked what I am doing.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Have you annexed any documents about the orders in the NMS case?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: When the governor first went to court about the legality or trying to withdraw from the Deed, I think Justice Wasilwa lifted that order. There was no order. If you went to appeal that is not---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are you aware that Petition E348 exists in the constitutional court about the NMS and its legality?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I am not aware.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are not aware? Have you not annexed any document in connection to that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I am not aware about any case.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Look at page 402 of your volume 1. There is a copy of a court order from the Hon. Justice Wasilwa dated 6th November 2020. Would you confirm that at page 402 and 403? Please confirm that an order was issued in Constitutional Petition E348 of 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am not party to all the issues he is raising. What I can confirm to this hon. House is that, I raised the issue of him not signing the warrant because we have the transferred functions, which have to be funded whether you are in court or not. Staff must be paid whether in court or not. It is not the issue of constitutionality.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Let me finish. We had asked for the video clip of the governor to be played in his witness statement from Mr. Moses Okerosi.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (There was a technical hitch while playing a video clip)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Would you confirm that, that video has been in reference to an appearance before the county assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: No, I do not know. I cannot confirm.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Volume 3 of the documents served on you on behalf of the Governor--- At Page 535 to 572, there is a response from the Governor to your allegations to the county assembly, in precision rebutting all the allegations. In the document marked (d), has Volume 1, 2 and 3. It has a blue cover; on page 535. The response on behalf of the Governor is dated 30th November, 2020; on page 535 to 572 of Volume 3. That document is signed by Ondieki Advocates.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, it is there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thereafter, you will see images on Page 633 to 643. You can see that the person who took the images has sworn an affidavit to confirm that he was actually there on the material date, that is, 3rd December, 2020. That is on Page 535-573 of Volume 3 of the statements. The images are on Page 633 to 643; Volume 3. Therefore, it is not true to allege that the Governor did not make an attempt to come to the county assembly on 3rd December, 2020.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, what I cannot confirm is what was transpiring on that particular day, because, one, the video was not audible. I could not hear. The other thing is that if he attempted to appear, then he must have had the notice and was invited.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Have you seen the affidavit of Moses Okerosi, which is along the same Volume 3? Have you seen it? Have you also seen the affidavit immediately after Page 643 in Volume 3, affirming that indeed they were there from 2.00 p.m. up to almost 5.00 p.m., and were denied access to the Nairobi City County Assembly? Sorry, we go to Volume 3; Page 633. There are images showing them being blocked outside the Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I can see the photographs.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You can see them?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: If you go to Volume 3, Pages 450 to 522, there is a report of an expert in handwriting refuting the signatures you were adducing that they had attained the majority. On page 450 is the affidavit of Emmanuel Kenga, a forensic document examiner, who has impugned your signatures. Have you seen that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I have not seen it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Look at page 450 of Volume Three. There is a sworn affidavit by Emmanuel Kenga, a forensic document examiner. He has said that he examined your signatures and he impugned them, some of which are a forgery. Have you seen that affidavit?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: At page 450? I can see it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Now, go to page 528, there is an affidavit of Moses Okerosi, who swears that he took that document to the County Assembly on behalf of the Governor and he was denied access. Have you seen that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes I can see it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, you can see His Excellency the Governor made every effort to be there on the material date, but he was denied access or audience. Now, you also allege that the Governor went to New York and got some payments made on his behalf. He has sworn an affidavit. At page 614, can you see a document there---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, for the record---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I want to conclude this. You will have an opportunity to be re-examined. Have a look at that document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order, let us hear him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, one thing I cannot confirm is what the photos speak to. I cannot confirm that he tried to come. Secondly, I have not said the Governor was in New York.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Okay, you alluded to his wife and daughter being in New York.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is not the Governor. I talked about the daughter.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: All right. At Volume Three, page 614, do you see the document there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I can see it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are you aware that the approval for the travel was actually from the Government of the Republic of Kenya? Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada
entries.text: For an imposter---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: No, are you aware that was sanctioned?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The letter that went to the Government was that, that was a sub-county administrator and yet the lady is not working for the county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have proof of that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, we have documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You do not have anything you can pin point.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have documents to that effect.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Let us look at Volume Two of the Governor's response affidavit, so that we save time. Let us look at page 297 running all the way up to page 311. Are you there?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Which page?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Page 297. Can you see that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, I can see.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You can see those are images of your colleagues, hon. Members of the Nairobi City County Assembly?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I can see some people.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Up to the last page 311, there are 57 of them in number. You can confirm that. You know that those Members of the County Assembly (MCAs) have each sworn an affidavit to say that they did not vote for the Motion to impeach the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, one thing we need to appreciate is that voting was online. So, if any Member swore such an affidavit, then they were playing you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You can see at page 200 there are single affidavits running all the way up to page 277. Each of them has sworn an affidavit to say that they did not vote on that day. Can you see that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I can see and we also have affidavits of the same people saying these are not their signatures.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You do not have that evidence before this---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have affidavits here of these people who---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: On page 278, this was reported to the Kwale Police Station as impersonation. Do you see they reported that? It is OB No.55 of 3rd December, 2020. Do you see that? Just confirm yes or no. Do you see evidence of reporting that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I really do not know how to answer yes or no. I need to be given time to explain myself. One thing that you need to appreciate is that the said Members of the County Assembly (MCAs) actually also reported to the police that they were kidnapped. They were invited to a house in Runda. Prados came and they were being forced two-two into a Prado. You could not alight.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I would like to play a video.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Let him finish what he is saying.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the same MCAs are saying they were invited to Runda and we have affidavits that they were going to be given Kshs500,000 each. With this kind of dry season, nobody could really resist--- When they went the gates were locked and Prados started coming and MCAs were being forced into a van. They were all being forced into vans because there were people who were really forcing them to enter. Affidavits are there to that effect. Actually them being in Kwale was against their wish. That is why you can see most of them were tagged and given these numbers. Nobody could accept to carry a tag if there was no threat.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Ogada, none of these is in your statement. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like to play a YouTube clip that I have requested the ICT on deep fakes. This witness played clips there on someone resembling Gov. Mike Sonko without a certificate of authenticity. Deepfakes from YouTube, I have requested so that then I can get more time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the certificates are there. Besides that, the affidavits are on 9 (f).

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Let me see those affidavits you are talking about.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: You have the copy of the yellow document there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: You said you were playing a video clip.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, these are not dated. I have seen them in Volume 1 and some of them are not darted. Some of them are not even having the names. I would like to draw your very kind attention to just one single of those affidavits so that we disabuse these honorable Members of the allegations that there are sworn statements. There are no such legally sworn affidavits. Unfortunately, the pagination is not proper. I cannot see the pagination. The honorable MCAs are here as well so that they can see. There is the affidavit of Mr. David Ayoyi. Do you have it there with you? You see it is not even dated. It is on Page 14. Ms. Elizabeth Nyambura is here and she has said that she never even affixed to such alleged signature. She did not. I am seeing Mr. Alvin Palapala also. These are honorable MCAs. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I wanted to play that clip in their presence. Those honorable MCAs are here. I wanted to play a clip to negate those video clips. I beg for an enlargement just of some little time. It was unfortunate. Kindly, Mr. Speaker, Sir, and honorable Members, bear with me. The clip that I have with the ICT, I had requested that they play the video clip from YouTube only from Deepfakes which is the source of it. Mr. Speaker, Sir, can I get your authority?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, thank you. ICT, I had sent a link from YouTube Deepfakes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: It is like they are not able to play it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, while they are checking it, let me just ask two questions. Mr. Ogada, you are aware that the County Government mandates public participation. You must give five days between the notice and the event. Are you aware of that? It is in the County Governments Act.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I am aware. It was done and put in the dailies.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text:
Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui\n(The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)

:

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor
entries.speaker_title: (Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui)
entries.text: Do you have proof of that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: They are in the dailies.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have proof of that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: There was.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, whom did you give the clip? Our records indicate that we do not have any clip from you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: It was a link.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Whom did you send to?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, for purposes of record, we were never served with that link and clip. That is new evidence being introduced on the bar.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: With tremendous respect, I have referred to the link in my volume---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: It ought to be part of your evidence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Yes, the video clip is part of the evidence. This is provided by His Excellency the Governor. There is the link of TV47 on page 15, volume one, paragraph 69. The link is provided there. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I want to confirm with you and hon. Members that I am not so dishonourable as to cite a link that I have not provided. I did provide. It is cited in paragraph 69, page 15 of volume one. I also provided the clip. Mr. Speaker, Sir, as we wait for that clip, allow me to pursue that issue of public participation. You have seen the affidavit of Mr. Newton Munene, supplied with his documents. Mr. Newton Munene, the Information Communication Technology (ICT) officer of the Nairobi City County Government refuted and disputed there was public participation as you suppose. I refer to his affidavit which we had filed and supplied. Mr. Newton Munene, in paragraph one says, "I am the current CEC in charge of ICT Department." He has sworn to it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: For the purposes of public participation, did we have to go through the Chief Executive Committee (CEC) Member in charge of ICT? That was meant for the public. It was not for the CEC in charge of ICT.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are having challenge with that issue. I wanted to refute the allegation that there was a majority of the Nairobi City County Assembly Members who voted for the purported impeachment. The threshold set in law was not met. That was the purpose of the clip. As I was winding up, the clip is there and the link is provided. Unfortunately, I find myself accosted with this handicap.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: They are working on it.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: While they are working on it, allow me to yield to my learned friend, Mr. Nyamu, so that he can---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for the Nairobi City County Assembly (Mr. Ashioya Biko Brian)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you had accorded them an additional 20 minutes. We did not complain. It is our time that they are eating into. By yielding, it is abusing that accommodation that you gave them.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, you have gone beyond the 20 minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, sir, the occasion has arisen because hon. Members wanted clarity. Hon. Members are so respectable. I would not want to override that desire for clarity. Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am so subservient to your leadership. However, His Excellency the Governor is pressed to demonstrate in refuting the allegations against him. He has not stolen the money. In fact, the bursary funds were stolen by MCAs. That documentation is here. That was necessary to be provided.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is what you should have started with.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The witness did not answer my questions. The witness was evasive.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I was never asked about the bursary.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The clip is playing now.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (A Video clip was played)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. You can see from that video clip you and your Honourable colleagues on the material day 3rd December 2020. Do you confirm? I had requested that they mute so that the witness can see and confirm that that was the event he spoke of at the County Assembly contemporaneous with what was happening with the other MCAs that have I have said.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, one thing I can confirm is that I know several members who are talking there. Alongside, you can see me also prosecuting that case. That was actually not during voting. During voting, they were not talking. That is when they were voting. When they were shouting, I was talking. Therefore, you can see. During voting, they were not shouting. If they would have been shouting during voting, that would have been a different case, but there you see me arguing my case there as they shout. After they finished shouting, they started voting. That is how it happened.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that you have no evidence that they voted?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: There is enough evidence. We have got the HANSARD and everything else. We have got enough evidence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that there is no HANSARD before this House?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have enough evidence within this House.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, allow me to have two minutes with Mr. Nyamu to ask about the Dandora issue.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, with your permission, you directed. Let us not abuse the privilege.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, they took so much time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Let me give Mr. Nyamu five minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we have split the minutes into two and three. I will ask a few questions, and then my colleague will conclude. Hon. Ogada, I know that you are a very hard-working officer. I am giving you a document, the Auditor-General's report for 2018/2019. Look at that report, Hon. Ogada. Go to page three of the Auditor-General's report. Hon. Ogada, read paragraph 2.0. What is the heading of paragraph 2.0 on page 3 at the bottom? Read the recommendation on page 3.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I can only see a list of Members of the County Assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I am asking you to look at page 3.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: A list of county assembly members. All members of the county assembly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Page 3 at the bottom.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ashioya Biko
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we might be informed of the document that is---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Read Paragraph 2.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, this document was not availed to us. It is a document being given to our client for the first time. It does not even emanate from our client. It emanates from the Office of the Auditor-General. It will be unfair for the witness to be asked questions or read a document that he is interacting with for the first time

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you made a determination that you would be flexible in terms of the rules of admissibility so that we move on. This is a report of the Auditor-General of Kenya where he has indicted the witness because he was paid Kshs1.2 million irregularly.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, what they are raising is that you had not submitted that document to them?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the evidence was submitted yesterday in our bundle of documents. I would just like to confirm that his name is there.

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Loud consultations)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The Counsel of Nairobi City County Assembly says that they are seeing the document for the first time now. Can you confirm that is true?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, there is an attempt to derail this case so that time continues running. You have given a ruling to which I propose that as you wisely stated, where the examination- in-chief is one hour then for purposes of cross-examination, we only have half that hour for the other party. You are gracious enough to let the part present their case and they are only taking us round in circles and circus. We do not have the document they are relying on and we cannot confirm the same. I, therefore, urge this House to do that which is honourable. Least of which, this House will have to go around the same circus. I beg to yield so that we get direction.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The Secretariat will check for the document in question and report whether it was received before today.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we stand guided. I would like to ask him about the bursaries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The Secretariat has confirmed that we do not have the document. Move on that is noted.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I would like Mr. Ogada to go to Page 157 of that documents where he states that the bursary lost.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the affidavit of the Governor served us ends at page merely Page 62.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, they are in volumes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Duncan Okatch
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the document I have is what was served as at yesterday when the documents were being exchanged. We are being taken round circus. My learned seniors should come clean on what they want to prosecute. They are not prosecuting the witness. They are prosecuting the Motion before this House. It is not perjuring the witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the Counsel of Nairobi City County Assembly served us new documents late at 6.00 p.m. We put in an affidavit in response and that is the one we are talking about. It was delivered to the Office of the Clerk of the Senate. We sought leave.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, looking at Page 167, you will see a voucher for Kshs297 million that is being talked about in bursaries.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we will run into serious problems here when counsel seeks to rely on documents that have not been served. We have no such documents served upon us and neither does this Senate have the opportunity of examining these documents because they are not before you. It will do us a great favour if we restrict ourselves to the documents served. We have no such documents.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, these documents will help the Senate appreciate issues that have been said that are lies.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: If that was the intention, they should have been served.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order! Was the document served?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we delivered all the documents to the Office of the Clerk which were served electronically to every party because of time constraints.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What is your point of order, Sen. Olekina?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I remember very clearly that you gave a directive that documents be brought to this House. If the counsel of the governor is referring to those documents, then we would like to have the documents. When they made an application, you stated that the documents be brought. If we can be given the documents, he can clarify. I remember discussing with my colleague, Sen. Orengo and saying that if the Speaker has accepted documents to be introduced in the House, can we have those documents so that we proceed? You allowed the documents to be introduced.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Did I? No.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: The HANSARD can bear me witness.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Which documents did I allow?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Ledama Olekina
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, when I listened to the counsel of the governor submitting, they indicated that they were served with the documents at 6.30 p.m., and they requested to be allowed to submit their responses to those submissions.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: If my memory serves me right, the documents were taken to the wrong place, then they were brought back later out of the time. This is when the Secretariat allowed documents. The documents they are asking for now, were they served? Were they part of the documents delivered later after delivering in the wrong place?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, it was one continuous bundle.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, we are the ones who received the bundles of documents. I believe your directions were only in respect to the documents that were served. The directions were in respect of the documents that were received not any other introduction of new evidence. You gave a ruling. We ask you to overrule.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, you guided us.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Aaron Kipkirui Cheruiyot
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, to help us, this is a simple and straightforward matter. To help us make way out of the dispute between the Assembly and the governor, the counsel of the governor should refer to all the documents presented to us as numbered. It will make sense every time they refer the counsel of Assembly to a particular document, they mention, so that we also confirm that this is the set of documents we have. That will end this dispute and we will easily understand whether they were served or not.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: What number is that document? Senator for Kericho says it will assist us.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, all the documents served from the governor's office are labelled as 'D', the document being referred to is labelled '1'. These are the documents that the clerk forwarded to us and had annexed it at the time of the service. This is an alien document.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am sorry, I had gone to the bathroom. I need to clarify that issue. If you need a record from the HANSARD, immediately upon your ruling, you asked that we proceed and I said I have a further plea. Now that the documents were served late at 6.30 p.m, and the HANSARD will record that, you said they can be accepted. I liaised with the staff and from the Clerk's office. I showed the email that I did communicate on that account and then you said you granted me. I am surprised that my learned friend is alleging they are strange documents. I did put the documents to this witness that are here. For instance, the payment to Nairobi City County Assembly that resulted in his refusal to answer. The documents about the Nairobi Metropolitan Services (NMS) are here. The more reason---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: ): No objection was raised.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I did refer. I said go to page such and such, and he went.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Order!

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Sorry, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I will check the HANSARD and get exactly what I said.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Again, if he was referring to documents that were not served, then that evidence should be expunged because we are not aware of this evidence.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, when it suites them, they say that this is an inquisitorial process. Now that we are presenting evidence before the honourable Senate, they say that they are objecting. This must be rejected.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Hon. Ogada, I want you to go to Page 167 of that document, please.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I agree with Sen. Cheruiyot that any documents that the county assembly or the Governor wants to use in prosecuting their case must be documents that are before us. If they are before us, they should refer us to those particular documents. If they are having a discussion between the two of them and we do not have those documents, it is highly irregular. I think that in the future, any document we receive must be stamped to signify the fact that they came to us. Part of the problem is that we did not stamp the documents. I really urge that either side should not ambush the other. If there are documents that they are referring to, they must be documents that are with us. They can then refer us to those documents. Otherwise, it is going to end up as a private discussion between the two of them.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is true. The hon. Senators do not have that document, and so they cannot refer.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The document is with the Clerk. It is here; they can give it to the Senators. We delivered it yesterday.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The documents came late. The advice that I have is that you can apply and refer to the documents tomorrow when you are presenting your case. Is that okay? Let us then proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I am sorry to interrupt. That application is what I made immediately and before Mr. Njiiru addressed you, and you said that it is okay; that they can be brought. I liaised with your Clerk.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The documents are not here with the hon. Senators yet.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Harrison Kinyanjui
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, they are here. I liaised with the Clerk and was given the affirmation. In fact, I can check the time that I sent the message.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: The Senators do not have it. Can we use them when you present your case tomorrow?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is better.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: This is so that the Senators can also look at the document. When you are presenting your case, you can refer to that document, which the Senators would have looked at.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Cherarkey K Samson
entries.text: On a point of order, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Cherargei.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Cherarkey K Samson
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, the implication of that is that they will have to stand down the witness as of now, so that when we have those copies and that information sufficiently available to us, it will be easy to refer to as the Counsel of the Governor will be prosecuting that matter. I think it will mean that you need to stand down the witness as at now, so that we can proceed tomorrow.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is fair and just.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Orengo.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: James Orengo
entries.speaker_title: (The Senate Minority Leader)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, since we do not have time, let them cross-examine the witness to the extent that they can and that level, the witness can be stood down only for that reason tomorrow, so that we do not open the witness again to other matters.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is fair, Mr. Speaker, Sir.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: That is what I was going to say, on that particular one only. Let us proceed. We have eaten into the time I gave you.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor (Mr. Wilfred Nyamu)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I will very briefly put questions to this witness with regard to procurement at Dandora, which is Ground No.1(J) where it is alleged that the Governor violated the Public Procurement and Disposal Act in relation to the contract at Dandora. Hon. Ogada, the document that I will ask you questions on is marked 9B. Kindly move to page 809, Ground 1(J).

entries.label: scene
entries.text: (Somebody consulted Hon. Ogada)

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor (Mr. Wilfred Nyamu)
entries.text:
Could you kindly get off that stand? I am waiting for you to get out of there. You have no business standing there.

Hon. Ogada, as an MCA of Nairobi City County Assembly, do you know who are the accounting officers of the respective county government entities?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I know.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Who are the accounting officers of the respective county government entities and who appoints them?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We may have several, but one particular one is the Head of the Treasury.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Who appoints accounting officers of the respective departments?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The County Executive Committee Member for Finance.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You confirm that is under Section 148 of the PFM Act?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You are aware that under Section 149 of the PFM Act they are the ones charged with the responsibly of procurement of goods and services? Right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In your allegation Ground No.1 (J), you alleged that the County Governor has violated the procurement law. Is that right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, as the CEO, he oversaw the violation.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You appreciate that the Governor does not deal with procurement matters.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: He does not deal with procurement matters, but I have said as the CEO, he is in charge and the buck stops with him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are you holding the Governor liable vicariously?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, any mess that happens to the Nairobi City County Government, he is personally---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: So, are you saying that if a Nairobi City County Government askari commits a mistake out there, the Governor is the one to blame?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: As a County Assembly, we will watch the footsteps of the Governor. If he does not take any action against a City County Government askari, then we will hold him personally accountable.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Are there situations whereby officers of the county Government have been charged with offences relating to their act or omissions and the Governor is not charged?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: In the documents that you have brought, which begin at page 809--- Hon. Speaker, I am referring to the black file marked 9B page 809. I will refer to page 809 all the way to page 811. Looking at Page 809, you look at that letter?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: To whom is that letter addressed?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: To Scanjet Construction.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Who is the author of the letter?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Abdi Mutalip Ibrahim.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: What position does he hold?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: County Chief Officer for Youth and Sports.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You confirm that the same is in relation to the stadium, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is the Dandora Stadium, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is that not a copy to the Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Just as I have said---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is it copied to the Governor, yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is their administrative issues which I cannot- --

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Answer my question. Is that letter copied to the Governor? Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: The way they work is an administration issue.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel of Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, our time is limited. That question calls for an answer in terms of yes or no.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It is copied to the County Secretary.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Is it copied to the Governor?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It is copied to the County Secretary who is the Chief Officer and generally the head of the public service with the Governor's government.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I am asking you whether the Governor is copied that letter. Yes or no?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: It is not copied to him but he is personally liable for the actions of his people.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is period. Now move to Page 810. This is your document. What does that particular document speak about? It speaks about Dandora Stadium. Is it not?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, it is about Dandora Stadium.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Does it mention the Governor anywhere?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I think I have just told you the Governor is the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the county. All the bucks stop with the Governor as the CEO of the county.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Answer my question.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Witness, you should just answer. It saves time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes. His name is not there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: The name of the Governor is not there.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Has he participated in the authorship of that document?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I cannot confirm that about the authorship.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: But you have not seen his involvement in that document, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: I have not seen a letter copied to him.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That particular document is by project architect Nairobi City County, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: You will agree with me that the construction of that stadium falls under a certain department where there is a county government accounting officer, right? That department is youths and sports, right? Why are you perusing? It is on Pages 810 and 811. The Dandora Stadium is a project under a county government entity. That is youths and sports. Did you confirm that?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: There is an accounting officer for purposes of procurement, right?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes. That is true.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Now, if there were any anomalies in relation to the procurement at Dandora Stadium, as a MCA of Nairobi, you have powers and authority to oversight and even call witnesses under Article 185. Is that an objection?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Ndegwa Njiiru
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Assembly)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, while I do not want to interrupt Mr. Nyamu, my senior, kindly indicate to us how much more time he has. He seems to have expended the five minutes you gave them between him and his brother, Mr. Ondieki. He does not have the luxury of time.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Proceed, I will give direction on that.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, maybe it is because I am asking questions that are pertinent. Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu, do you know and appreciate that you have powers and latitude under Article 185 of the Constitution to oversight officers of the county?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, that what we have been doing and it is extension of why I am here. We are oversighting.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Have you ever sought to summon the accounting officer for that particular department?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Several times. That is why we have to deal with the master.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have any records in these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Counsel, Mr. Wilfred Nyamu, I will give you five minutes.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Very well, Mr. Speaker, Sir. I appreciate. While Mr. Ndegwa is trying to coach you, hon. Michael Ogada Okumu, do you have any evidence here that you exercise the power to oversight such an officer and now that you have to go for the master?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have overwhelming evidence of summoning the officers.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have it here?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We have overwhelming evidence. That is why we decided since the buck stops with the boss, as a City County Assembly, we had no option, but to deal with the boss.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have it on record in these proceedings?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Basically, that is not a matter---

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: Sen. Madzayo, what is your intervention?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: That is not a matter before us.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Stewart Mwachiru Shadrack Madzayo
entries.text: Thank you, Mr. Speaker, Sir. Normally when a lawyer is cross- examining and he asks you a question, just say 'yes' or 'no.' I believe the witness should do so instead of trying to be evasive from whatever angle. It does not save time. Could you be kind enough to guide the witness to reply with a 'yes' or 'no' answer? That is exactly what the witness should do. I do not think we need any extra issues.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Lusaka
entries.speaker_title: (The Speaker)
entries.text: I have said that more than 50 times. The witness should save us time on that. Let us proceed.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have any evidence of exercise of your oversight role as an MCA in relation to these particular projects against the accounting officer or the departmental head?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Yes, we have.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you have it here?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: That is under the ability of the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: I am asking you whether or not you have it. Say 'yes' or 'no'?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: We are prosecuting the Governor.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
entries.speaker_title: (The Counsel for Nairobi City County Governor)
entries.text: Do you confirm that you do not have any evidence of summoning or raising any questions in relation to these projects to any departmental head?

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Hon. Michael Ogada Okumu
entries.text: Mr. Speaker, Sir, I have said we have done that. There is a report from the Committee.

entries.label: speech
entries.speaker: Mr. Wilfred Nyamu
